attrs.summary: Prioritize geopolitical risk on the Taiwan‑sourced GPU chip and currency moves on German, Japanese, and South Korean components to protect the largest cost exposures.

attrs.reason: P001 accounts for 58% of spend (GBP 1,057,350) from Taiwan; recent headlines on the U.S. and allies joining forces on chips and Taiwan export controls raise compliance‑cost risk, so a geopolitics analyst can estimate the % cost change.
P006 is 14% of spend (GBP 247,041) from Germany; EUR/GBP FX data is available from the ECB, and the headline BoE 50‑bp hike plus UK recession risk drives currency‑move cost impact.
P003 represents 6% of spend (GBP 103,973) from Japan; JPY/GBP FX data is ECB‑available, and the same macro‑headlines make JPY volatility relevant to part cost.
P002 comprises 5% of spend (GBP 96,746) from South Korea; KRW/GBP FX data is ECB‑available, and the headline on U.S./ally chip controls adds risk that could affect part pricing.
P004 is only 4% of spend (GBP 68,610) from China; China‑related FX data exists but the part’s low spend does not warrant a dedicated delegation.
P005 is 3% of spend (GBP 62,156) from China; similar low‑spend argument as P004.
P007 is 7% of spend (GBP 122,233) from China; although FX data is available, the part’s risk is already captured by the Taiwan‑focused geopolitics delegation, and spend is modest relative to P001.
P008 is 3% of spend (GBP 57,688) from Malaysia; MYR FX data is not guaranteed ECB‑covered, and the part’s low spend makes it a lower priority.
